title: Terrain level 3x the size of daggerfall 2x of UK, loading instantly and rendering fast in browser
author: Accomplished-Fan9568
selftext:
A landmass of 580x840km, a square tile of 1024x1024 km

  
Terrain level three times the size of daggerfall, twice the size of UK loading and rendering instantly in browser!

I think it has great potential for RPGs, hope u guys like it!

comments.author: davesoft
comments.body: Nice. I'm dabbling with 'gigantic' worlds for a kenshi clone, without proc gen and chunking it would be trapped at 3 frames a second. The zoom out at the end is impressive, 'mine' looks alot simpler than that when zooming out, not enough altitude variety compared to yours.

replies.author: wam_bam_mam
replies.body: That is where attentive ai comes in to play, you tell it this is the general theme of the lands, come up with the following density in story telling, tell it there has to be a overall branching narrative, create the NPCs assign the dialogs and describe any cut scenes.

replies.author: Agreeable-Safety-360
replies.body: You'd be better off doing what successful devs have done when making large game worlds/ universes, and make the game systems based. Games like cdda, stellaris, kenshi, dwarf fortress. All these games are like...pretty shallow with NPC interactivity and story, even the world building  can be a little mid depending on the game you're talking about. But one thing they a have in common are very deep and complex systems that all work together. They help drive the world and npcs that allow you as the player to interact with things differently. The game itself becomes more about the player making their own story.
